question: Dispersion of white light through a glass prism takes place because:

options.text: the prism absorbs some colours and transmits others
different colours travel with different speeds in glass
different colours travel with the same speed in glass
white light splits due to reflection inside the prism

solution:
The correct answer is __**different colours travel with different speeds in glass**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Dispersion of light** occurs when **white light splits into its constituent colours** (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, and Red) as it passes through a glass prism.
 
• This phenomenon happens because **different colours of light have different wavelengths**, and the refractive index of the glass varies with wavelength.
 
• As a result, **different colours travel at different speeds** in the glass, causing them to bend by different amounts. Violet bends the most, while Red bends the least.
 
• The varying degree of bending (refraction) leads to the separation of colours, creating the spectrum of light.
 
• The **prism shape** plays a critical role as the non-parallel surfaces cause the light to refract at different angles.
